propositions: The enrich drain gate check on every ticket write walks all ticket directories and performs O(ticket_count) reduce_ticket calls, each scanning event files three times, resulting in ~24,000 metadata syscalls that take 486-740 ms against a declared 20 ms budget.
On a quiet store (no pending enrichment), a repeated gate probe should return immediately without reducing any tickets, but currently rescans the entire store every time.
Under concurrent write workloads, gate checks contend on vnode cache saturation, causing write latency to scale with the number of simultaneous gate walkers rather than store size alone.
The gate's budget-breach warning fires on 100% of writes to stores with >150 tickets, making it noise and hiding genuine breaches; it should fire rarely if at all on ordinary writes.
An O(1) marker under .rebar tracking next_eligible_ns can prove store quietness without a full scan, with self-healing via TTL expiration and invalidation on queue mutations.
